newsitem.title: TURKEY: Erbakan aims for Turkish lira parity with dollar.
newsitem.headline: Erbakan aims for Turkish lira parity with dollar.

text.p: Turkey's Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Tuesday the government was working on plans to relaunch the Turkish lira at a rate of one to one against the U.S. dollar.
"Work is being carried out in connection with making one Turkish lira equal to one dollar and keeping it steady," Erbakan told a meeting of his Islamist Welfare Party.
He did not refer to previous suggestions that a new Turkish currency could be introduced as part of efforts to counter the currency's rapid devaluation.

The Turkish lira was quoted at 97,140 liras per dollar on Tuesday. The lira has lost around 40 percent of its value against the dollar since the start of the year and annual inflation in Turkey is around 80 percent.
In his speech to party members, Erbakan reiterated that the government was aiming for a balanced budget in 1997 -- a forecast about which analysts are highly sceptical.
"Our priority is not to become indebted once more...The debts incurred before us we will pay back coin by coin," the Islamist leader said.

He said there were possibilities to expand the country's ambitious privatisation programme, which has made slow progress since its initiation 10 years ago. The government aims to raise $3.5 billion from the sale of telecommunications company Turk Telekom and a further $4.1 billion from other sell-offs in 1997.
Power stations and dams could also be sold off to raise around $2.5 billion while helping to solve the problem of meeting Turkey's growing energy demand, Erbakan said.
He said talks were being held on ways to promote the domestic defence industry, noting that 80 percent of an annual $9 billion spent on defence goes to foreign companies.
